# Source decision, routing and capability register

Version: 1.0.0

Date: 2026-10-19

Status: static coverage obligations; none are execution receipts

This is the loss-prevention appendix to [the design](README.md) and [operation inventory](paths.md). It keeps declared destinations and decision anchors visible so small branches cannot vanish inside a broad happy-path label. Rows retain current source wording even when it conflicts with the new public surface.

A register row is not automatically one standalone test. Attach it to an operation case and enumerate its behavioral outcomes; repeated instructions may share a case. Templates, parser implementation details and informational tables need an explicit nonbehavioral disposition. Unresolved references and contradictory contracts stay open. Static extraction cannot prove model reachability or eliminate implicit model decisions. The closure review must check both missed decisions and overinclusive entries.

## Hook event routes

Every row requires an actual matching-event run, a nonmatching run, an inactive-project run, and applicable failure cases from the design.

| Event | Matcher | Hook |
|---|---|---|
| SessionStart | `startup` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/session-preflight.sh` |

## Model/agent dispatch

Every configured role must dispatch to its configured model; absent role uses default. A provider/model failure must propagate to the owning workflow without substituted completion. Agents are exercised through legitimate workflows, not by asking the test driver to perform their work.

```yaml
default: claude-sonnet-4-6
routes:
  brainstorming: claude-opus-4-6
  architecture: claude-opus-4-6
  prd-review: claude-opus-4-6
  reasoning-frameworks: claude-opus-4-6
  test-writing: claude-sonnet-4-6
  implementation: claude-sonnet-4-6
  fix-issue: claude-sonnet-4-6
  gherkin-bridge: claude-sonnet-4-6
  code-review: claude-sonnet-4-6
  security-review: claude-sonnet-4-6
  workflow-guardian: claude-sonnet-4-6
  test-runner: claude-haiku-4-5
  auto-test: claude-haiku-4-5
  ripple-scan: claude-haiku-4-5
  auto-docs: claude-haiku-4-5
  qa-caucus-service: claude-sonnet-4-6
  qa-caucus-component: claude-sonnet-4-6
  qa-caucus-integration: claude-sonnet-4-6
```

Agents: `agents/architecture-reviewer.md`, `agents/code-reviewer.md`, `agents/implementer.md`, `agents/performance-reviewer.md`, `agents/qa-caucus-component.md`, `agents/qa-caucus-integration.md`, `agents/qa-caucus-service.md`, `agents/security-reviewer.md`, `agents/test-writer.md`, `agents/tests-reviewer.md`, `agents/workflow-guardian.md`.

## Workflow phase paths

Each phase edge needs pass, missing-precondition, rejected-advance, and invalid-order coverage. Cold-start/planned/reactive entry and every progressive-disclosure stage are separate fixtures.

| Work type | Entry categories | Ordered phases | Hard gates / post-ship |
|---|---|---|---|
| `net-new-feature` | cold-start, mid-project-planned | DISCOVER → DEFINE → DESIGN → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `external-integration` | cold-start, mid-project-planned | DISCOVER → DEFINE → DESIGN → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `course-correction` | mid-project-planned, mid-project-reactive | DISCOVER → DEFINE → TRIAGE → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `security-planning` | cold-start, mid-project-planned | DISCOVER → DEFINE → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `enhancement` | mid-project-planned | DEFINE → DESIGN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `tech-debt` | mid-project-planned | DEFINE → SCOPE → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `compliance-requirement` | mid-project-planned, mid-project-reactive | ASSESS → DEFINE → DESIGN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `infrastructure-change` | mid-project-planned | DEFINE → DESIGN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {"DESIGN": "Solutioning gate required at GA+. Rollback plan must exist before DESIGN completes."}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `onboarding-flow-design` | mid-project-planned | DEFINE → DESIGN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `release-planning` | mid-project-planned | DEFINE → PLAN → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `bug-fix` | mid-project-planned, mid-project-reactive | DIAGNOSE → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `security-patch` | mid-project-planned, mid-project-reactive | DIAGNOSE → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {"VERIFY": "Security review mandatory before SHIP. No soft bypass."}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `performance-optimization` | mid-project-planned | DIAGNOSE → DESIGN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `rollback-revert` | mid-project-reactive | DIAGNOSE → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": "POST-MORTEM"} |
| `technology-migration` | mid-project-planned | ASSESS → DESIGN → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → CUTOVER → CLEANUP | {"hard_gates": {"DESIGN": "Solutioning gate required at GA+.", "CUTOVER": "Human decision required. Explicit confirmation logged to decision log. No soft bypass."}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `data-migration` | mid-project-planned | ASSESS → DESIGN → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {"VERIFY": "Integrity checks mandatory (row counts, checksums, sample records). No soft bypass.", "ASSESS": "Solutioning gate + Change impact analysis required at GA+."}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `api-deprecation` | mid-project-planned | ASSESS → DEFINE → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP → CLEANUP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `dependency-upgrade` | mid-project-planned, mid-project-reactive | ASSESS → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → SHIP | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": null} |
| `hotfix` | mid-project-reactive | DIAGNOSE → IMPLEMENT → SHIP → POST-MORTEM | {"hard_gates": {}, "post_ship_spawn": "POST-MORTEM"} |

## Mode rules

Test each rule independently plus its caller-side explanation and actual tool enforcement. All directed mode changes are also required.

```yaml
schema_version: 1
mode_defaults:
  flow:
    default_tdd_level: 1
    wip_limit: null
    cycle_duration_weeks: null
    blocked_skills: []
    gates: []
  kanban:
    default_tdd_level: 1
    wip_limit: 3
    cycle_duration_weeks: null
    blocked_skills:
    - project-sprints
    gates:
    - phase: IMPLEMENT
      condition: wip_limit_reached
      action: block
      message: WIP limit reached ({current}/{limit} items in_progress). Complete or
        move an item before starting new work.
  shape_up:
    default_tdd_level: 2
    wip_limit: null
    cycle_duration_weeks: 6
    blocked_skills:
    - project-sprints
    - project-backlog
    gates:
    - phase: IMPLEMENT
      requires: betting_table_approved
      action: block
      message: Work must be pitched and bet before implementation begins. Run /sweetclaude:project-issues
        to create issues from a pitch.
    - phase: VERIFY
      condition: ship_no_ship_decision
      action: required
      message: Ship/no-ship decision required. Did the core outcome land within appetite?
    - phase: PLAN
      condition: issues_from_backlog
      action: block
      message: Shape Up has no backlog. Issues must be derived from an approved pitch.
  agile:
    default_tdd_level: 2
    wip_limit: null
    cycle_duration_weeks: null
    blocked_skills: []
    gates:
    - phase: IMPLEMENT
      condition: no_active_sprint
      action: block
      message: No active sprint. Run /sweetclaude:project-sprints start to activate
        a sprint.
    - phase: IMPLEMENT
      condition: issue_not_in_sprint
      action: warn
      message: This issue is not assigned to the active sprint. Assign it or start
        a new sprint.
    - phase: SHIP
      condition: sprint_complete
      action: prompt
      message: All sprint issues are done. Run sprint close before shipping.
```

## Migration, skill lifecycle and disclosure registries

These are fixture/branch inputs. Every registered chain edge requires success, missing handler, handler failure, snapshot failure, refused approval, replay/resume and rollback paths; skill feature states require uninitialized/active/paused and declared dependency paths.

```yaml
migration-registry:
  schema_version: 1
  state_files:
    phase.yaml:
      description: Active phase, work item, version stage, deference level
      current_version: 2
      backup_required: true
      consolidated_into: sweetclaude.yaml
      expected_absent_when:
        target_file_exists: sweetclaude.yaml
      migrations:
      - from: 1
        to: 2
        description: Separated version_stage from active_work_item; added work type
          + workflow template
        handler: phase_yaml_v1_to_v2
        implemented_in: scripts/migrations/phase_yaml_v1_to_v2.py
        validation:
          required_fields:
          - schema_version
          - version_stage
          - deference_level
          required_version: 2
    skills.yaml:
      description: Onboarding state for the six data-owning skills
      current_version: 2
      backup_required: false
      optional: true
      migrations:
      - from: 1
        to: 2
        description: Replaced enabled boolean with three-state status (active/paused/uninitialized);
          added last_changed_at and last_changed_by
        handler: skills_yaml_v1_to_v2
        implemented_in: scripts/migrations/skills_yaml_v1_to_v2.py
        validation:
          required_fields:
          - schema_version
          required_version: 2
    sweetclaude.yaml:
      description: "Unified project state \u2014 framework metadata, project metadata,\
        \ work state, features, drift findings"
      current_version: 2
      backup_required: true
      migrations:
      - from: 1
        to: 2
        description: Decline-state amnesty + stale discovery cleanup. Clears legacy
          boolean declined to null, clears stale update.available if older than installed_version,
          clears stale update.check_error.
        handler: sweetclaude_yaml_v1_to_v2
        implemented_in: scripts/migrations/sweetclaude_yaml_v1_to_v2.py
        validation:
          required_fields:
          - schema_version
          required_version: 2
    project.yaml:
      description: Language, framework, test runner, build commands
      current_version: 1
      backup_required: false
      migrations: []
    john-wick.yaml:
      description: John Wick autonomous pipeline state
      current_version: 1
      backup_required: true
      migrations: []
    corpus-pipeline.yaml:
      description: Document corpus pipeline state
      current_version: 1
      backup_required: false
      migrations: []
  backup_policy:
    path_template: .sweetclaude/state/backups/pre-migration-{date}-{sha7}.tar.gz
    retain_last_n: 5
skills-registry:
  schema_version: 1
  skills:
    product-milestones:
      description: Roadmap targets
      data_signal: '{base_path}/roadmap/milestones/MS-*.md'
      dependencies: []
    epics:
      description: Epic and objective management
      data_signal: '{base_path}/roadmap/epics/EP-*.md'
      dependencies: []
    product-parking-lot:
      description: Deferred work items
      data_signal: '{base_path}/backlog/ISSUE-*.md'
      dependencies: []
    product-sprint-plan:
      description: Sprint planning
      data_signal: null
      dependencies:
      - product-parking-lot
    user-personas:
      description: User personas
      data_signal: .sweetclaude/state/personas.yaml
      dependencies: []
    product-user-stories:
      description: User stories
      data_signal: '{base_path}/roadmap/issues/ISSUE-*.md'
      dependencies:
      - user-personas
    document-corpus:
      description: Document corpus
      data_signal: .sweetclaude/state/corpus-pipeline.yaml
      dependencies: []
progressive_disclosure:
  PROTOTYPE:
    visible_buckets:
    - strategy
    - product
  ALPHA:
    visible_buckets:
    - strategy
    - product
    - design
    - code
    core_implementation_work_types:
    - net-new-feature
    - bug-fix
    - external-integration
  BETA:
    visible_buckets:
    - strategy
    - product
    - design
    - code
    - operations
  GA:
    visible_buckets:
    - all
  SCALED:
    visible_buckets:
    - all
    surface_prominently:
    - operations
  MAINTAINED:
    visible_buckets:
    - code
    - operations
    available_work_types:
    - bug-fix
    - security-patch
    - dependency-upgrade
    - compliance-requirement
    de_emphasize:
    - feature-work
entry_categories:
  cold-start:
    description: New project, no prior context.
    behavior: Run full discovery pipeline. No prerequisites checked.
    entry_tasks:
    - net-new-feature
    - external-integration
    - security-planning
    - course-correction
  mid-project-planned:
    description: Continuing work, following the pipeline.
    behavior: "Classify \u2192 check prerequisites \u2192 flag gaps as advisory \u2192\
      \ offer to create missing artifacts \u2192 proceed."
    entry_tasks:
    - net-new-feature
    - enhancement
    - sprint-planning
    - backlog-management
    - user-feedback-triage
    - onboarding-flow-design
    - release-planning
    - tech-debt
    - security-patch
    - performance-optimization
    - external-integration
    - technology-migration
    - api-deprecation
    - data-migration
    - infrastructure-change
    - compliance-requirement
    - course-correction
  mid-project-reactive:
    description: Something happened that demands immediate response.
    behavior: Skip all prerequisite checks. Triage questions only. Proceed immediately.
      Offer missing prerequisites as optional parallel work.
    entry_tasks:
    - bug-fix
    - hotfix
    - something-broke
    - rollback-revert
    - security-patch
    - user-feedback-triage
    - course-correction
hard_gate_policy:
  soft_gate_escape: "I've addressed this informally [optional note] \u2014 proceed."
  hard_gate_override: User must explicitly confirm risk acceptance. Override logged
    to decision log.
  hard_gates_apply_at:
  - GA
  - SCALED
  - MAINTAINED
  hard_gate_tasks:
  - task: data-migration
    prerequisites:
    - solutioning-gate
    - change-impact-analysis
    reason: 'Blast radius: production data loss'
  - task: infrastructure-change
    prerequisites:
    - solutioning-gate
    - change-impact-analysis
    - rollback-plan
    reason: 'Blast radius: outage, data loss'
  - task: technology-migration
    prerequisites:
    - solutioning-gate
    - change-impact-analysis
    - parallel-run-plan
    reason: 'Blast radius: production instability'
  - task: security-patch
    prerequisites:
    - security-review-post-fix
    reason: Cannot ship an unreviewed security fix
```

## Capability paths

Each of the following manifest capabilities is a separate declared contract. Its delegate must be reconciled with the current category/index and mapped to an operation above. Exercise every supported project shape and unsupported-state disposition; verify declared preconditions, mutations, approval, postconditions and rollback limits. Older slash commands in this snapshot are compatibility/reachability obligations, not authorization to expose another public command.

Project shapes:

```yaml
recovery_required:
  guard_status: run-recover
  migrate_allowed: false
  message: This project is in a recoverable SweetClaude migration/update state. Run
    /sweetclaude:recover before any taxonomy migration.
  recovery_route: stabilize-without-migration
  recovery_capability: recover.stabilize_without_migration
manual_escalation:
  guard_status: manual-review
  migrate_allowed: false
  message: This project needs manual SweetClaude recovery review before migration
    or other maintenance commands.
  doctor_capability: doctor.manual_review
accepted_legacy_taxonomy:
  guard_status: compatibility-mode
  migrate_allowed: true
  message: This project has a legacy taxonomy layout. Run /sweetclaude:migrate to
    convert to v4, or /sweetclaude:recover to check graduation eligibility.
  migration_capability: migrate.typed_legacy_backlog
  graduation_capability: recover.graduate_from_compatibility
graduation_candidate:
  guard_status: graduation-available
  migrate_allowed: false
  message: This project is v4-compliant and can graduate from compatibility mode.
  graduation_capability: recover.graduate_from_compatibility
graduation_blocked:
  guard_status: graduation-blocked
  migrate_allowed: false
  message: This project could graduate from compatibility mode, but validation blockers
    must be fixed first. Each blocker carries its resolution.
  blocker_fix_capability: doctor.fix_graduation_blockers
  graduation_capability: recover.graduate_from_compatibility
flat_bl_backlog:
  migration: flat_bl_to_issue
  guard_status: migration-may-be-needed
  migrate_allowed: true
  message: Old-format work items were found and no recovery-only state was detected.
    Review /sweetclaude:migrate before executing it.
  migration_capability: migrate.flat_bl_to_issue
typed_legacy_backlog:
  guard_status: supported-migration-available
  migrate_allowed: true
  migration_capability: migrate.typed_legacy_backlog
  message: This project has a typed legacy backlog layout. Run /sweetclaude:migrate
    to migrate to the unified ISSUE-NNN taxonomy.
missing_product_base:
  guard_status: missing-product-base
  migrate_allowed: false
  message: SweetClaude product artifacts were not found. Run /sweetclaude:doctor or
    /sweetclaude:setup instead of migration.
  doctor_capability: doctor.manual_review
current_layout:
  guard_status: ok
  migrate_allowed: false
  message: No SweetClaude migration or recovery guard is currently active.
```

### Capability `recover.stabilize_without_migration`

```yaml
title: Stabilize recoverable legacy layout without taxonomy migration
delegate_skill: sweetclaude:recover
command_entrypoint:
  slash_command: /sweetclaude:recover
  script: scripts/recovery/recover_project.py
  module: recovery.recover_project
supports_project_shapes:
- recovery_required
mutation_class: planned_write
mutates_project: true
requires_approval: true
required_preconditions:
- project guard status is run-recover
- recovery plan exists before execute
snapshot_scope_hints:
- .sweetclaude/
- docs/product/
postconditions:
- id: recovery-postconditions
  check: recovery verifier reports stabilized state
rollback_support:
  supported: true
  command: python3 scripts/recovery/recover_project.py rollback --project-dir <project>
  limitations: []
unsupported_states:
- condition: manual_escalation
  behavior: escalate
- condition: missing_product_base
  behavior: diagnose_only
version_metadata:
  introduced_in: 4.1.0-beta
  deprecated_in: null
safety_contract:
- diagnose
- plan
- snapshot
- verify-snapshot
- approve
- execute
- record-progress
- resume
- verify-postconditions
- rollback
verification_commands:
- python3 scripts/recovery/recover_project.py diagnose --project-dir <project>
- python3 scripts/recovery/recover_project.py plan --project-dir <project>
```

```yaml
- user approval is bound to current plan

- .sweetclaude/state/

  behavior: block
- condition: recovery_required
  behavior: diagnose_only
- condition: manual_escalation
  behavior: escalate

  introduced_in: 4.0.0-beta
  deprecated_in: null
safety_contract:
- diagnose
- preflight
- plan
- snapshot
- approve
- execute
- verify-postconditions
- rollback
```


### Capability `recover.graduate_from_compatibility`

```yaml
title: Graduate from compatibility mode
supported: true
delegate_skill: sweetclaude:recover
command_entrypoint:
  slash_command: /sweetclaude:doctor
  script: scripts/recovery/recover_project.py
  module: recovery.recover_project
supports_project_shapes:
- accepted_legacy_taxonomy
- typed_legacy_backlog
- graduation_candidate
mutation_class: planned_write
mutates_project: true
requires_approval: true
required_preconditions:
- project is in compatibility mode or accepted legacy taxonomy
- graduation-check passes (v4-compliant)
snapshot_scope_hints:
- .sweetclaude/state/sweetclaude.yaml
postconditions:
- id: graduation-state-written
  check: recovery.taxonomy.status is graduated and framework.migration_status is complete
rollback_support:
  supported: true
  command: python3 scripts/recovery/recover_project.py rollback-graduation --project-dir <project>
  limitations: []
unsupported_states:
- condition: old_prefix_files_remain
  behavior: block
- condition: duplicate_ids
  behavior: block
- condition: frontmatter_parse_errors
  behavior: block
version_metadata:
```

## Source decision anchors

For prose and code conditions: enumerate true/false and each named status/choice; for loops: zero/one/many and bounded failure/retry; for tables: every selectable row. A source heading supplies location/ownership, not an automatic assertion that every sentence under it is a new branch. The JSON contains a structured copy with required outcomes and currently unmapped status.

| Anchor ID | Owner | Current decision or section |
|---|---|---|
| `section:CLAUDE.md:1` | `shared` | # Global Development Rules |
| `section:CLAUDE.md:3` | `shared` | ## Accuracy and honesty |
| `prose:CLAUDE.md:6` | `shared` | - If uncertain, say "I need to verify this" — never guess confidently. |
| `prose:CLAUDE.md:7` | `shared` | - If you catch an inconsistency mid-response, stop and correct it explicitly. |
| `section:CLAUDE.md:10` | `shared` | ## Session discipline |
| `prose:CLAUDE.md:13` | `shared` | - If resuming work, read \`.sweetclaude/plans/\` and recent git history before acting. |
| `section:CLAUDE.md:16` | `shared` | ## Global invariants |
| `prose:CLAUDE.md:18` | `shared` | - Never commit secrets, credentials, or API keys. If you spot them in a diff, stop and flag. |
| `section:CLAUDE.md:24` | `shared` | ## Credential safety |
| `prose:CLAUDE.md:26` | `shared` | - If you encounter what looks like a real secret, API key, token, or credential anywhere — in a file, grep output, diff, or log — **stop immediately and tell the user it exists. Never reproduce the value in your response, never quote it, never echo it.** Flag the location only. |
| `prose:CLAUDE.md:27` | `shared` | - Never read the contents of \`.env\`, \`.env.*\`, \`*.pem\`, \`*.p12\`, \`id_rsa\`, \`credentials\`, \`~/.aws/credentials\`, or any file whose name suggests it holds secrets. If a task requires knowing what's in such a file, tell the user to check it themselves. |

This applies whether or not the project is already configured. |

| `section:config/controls-map.md:277` | `shared` | ## Rejected Or Non-Standalone Controls |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:281` | `shared` | \| Idea \| Decision \| Reason \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:283` | `shared` | \| Generic supervisor approval \| Reject as standalone \| Human approval without evidence packet and blocking disposition recreates review theater. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:284` | `shared` | \| Raw stage-gate prompts \| Reject as standalone \| Cadence is useful, but prompts do not enforce state transitions. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:285` | `shared` | \| Promise documents that restate canon \| Reject by default \| They increase contradiction surface unless they add a distinct decision/control. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:286` | `shared` | \| Checkpoint existence \| Reject as restore proof \| Must include scope, restore command, and validation. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:287` | `shared` | \| Version label or branch name alone \| Reject as release identity \| Must be bound to tag, commit, package/plugin metadata, channel, and install path. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:288` | `shared` | \| "Tests passed" alone \| Reject as completion evidence \| Must map to objective criteria, contract, invariant, or postcondition. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:289` | `shared` | \| Provider failover without approval \| Reject \| Different model/provider behavior is a product decision, not hidden plumbing. \| |

| `section:config/controls-map.md:359` | `shared` | ## Design Risks |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:361` | `shared` | \| Risk \| Impact \| Mitigation \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:363` | `shared` | \| Overbuilding the receipt system \| Delays release-safety work \| Start with one common receipt schema and command-specific minimal extensions. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:364` | `shared` | \| Controls become advisory prose again \| Recreates current failure mode \| Each implementation story must name the transition it blocks and the failing fixture. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:365` | `shared` | \| Manifest resolver becomes another version table \| Reintroduces version chasing \| Capabilities must describe supported behavior and project shape, not release-specific scripts only. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:366` | `shared` | \| Human review still rubber-stamps \| False confidence \| Review packet isolation plus finding disposition gates make review findings transition-blocking. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:367` | `shared` | \| Checkpoint/restore proof is expensive \| Mutation work slows down \| Use fixture/dry-run restore proof first; require full round-trip only for high-risk mutations. \| |
| `table:config/controls-map.md:368` | `shared` | \| Provider observability distracts \| Scope creep \| Keep L6 deferred unless a future story explicitly accepts it. \| |

| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:1` | `shared` | # SweetClaude Interaction Model |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:5` | `shared` | ## Deference Levels |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:7` | `shared` | At session start, determine the deference level. If not set in \`state/phase.yaml\`, ask: |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:16` | `shared` | ## Phase Dwelling |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:26` | `shared` | **Not covered by this rule:** surfacing a separate finding and offering to act on it — "worth a backlog item if you want", "say the word and I'll file that". That is not phase advancement; the current work stays where it is, and a decision is handed to the user rather than taken from them. Other rules require it. Do not suppress findings to avoid tripping this one. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:30` | `shared` | ## Propose and Challenge |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:32` | `shared` | Default interaction mode is propose, not ask. Instead of "what do you think about X?" say "here's what I think about X — [reasoning]. Push back if this is wrong." |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:34` | `shared` | Include your reasoning so the user can evaluate your thinking, not just your conclusion. When the user corrects you, incorporate the correction immediately and acknowledge what you learned. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:36` | `shared` | ## Bounded Decisions Use the Menu |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:49` | `shared` | **"Something else" is always required — no exceptions.** Bounded decisions that look complete on the screen are never actually complete — the user often has a direction the framework didn't anticipate. The escape hatch is mandatory. If the user picks Something else, follow Adaptive Flow: drop the menu, follow their direction, track the original proposal so you can offer to return to it later. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:53` | `shared` | ## Status Changes — User Intent and Cascade Offer |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:55` | `shared` | A user's explicit status change is authoritative. Never silently revert it, and never let automated derivation (parent/child roll-up, doctor sync, controllers) override it. A milestone's or epic's status is *intent*, not a mechanical function of its children: a milestone can be \`active\` before any child is, an epic can be \`done\` with follow-on issues still open, and a parent can be \`on-hold\` regardless of its children. When you change a status on the user's behalf, route it through \`status.py\` (which records \`source: manual\` for user-initiated CLI changes) so the change is protected. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:59` | `shared` | ## Adaptive Language |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:61` | `shared` | Match your vocabulary to the user's vocabulary. If they use simple, non-technical language, respond in kind. If they use domain-specific terms (legal, medical, marketing), adopt their domain language. Never introduce framework terminology (phase gates, deference levels, TDD levels, exit criteria) unless the user has already used it or the context requires it. |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:63` | `shared` | When a framework concept is necessary, explain it in the user's terms first: "I'm going to write a description of what this feature should do before building it, so we can check that it works" rather than "We'll generate Gherkin acceptance tests for TDD Level 3." If the user demonstrates technical fluency, match it — don't oversimplify for someone who doesn't need it. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:67` | `shared` | ## Early-Phase Depth Rules (Discover and Define) |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:75` | `shared` | **Concrete examples required.** For problem statements, user descriptions, and success criteria, always ask for a specific scenario or real-world example if the user hasn't provided one. Abstract framing ("users want X") is not sufficient — ground it in a specific person doing a specific thing. |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:79` | `shared` | **Autonomous does not mean shallow.** At Autonomous deference, SweetClaude conducts the full interview internally — generating probing questions and answering them from available context — then presents a complete draft that meets the structural requirements from the phase gates. The draft is presented for user review. If phase gate exit criteria fail, pause and present findings even in Autonomous mode. "Stop only at phase gates" means phase gates are the one place Autonomous mode always pauses. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:81` | `shared` | ## Adaptive Flow |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:83` | `shared` | When the user redirects (stops you, changes topic, edits files directly, asks a tangential question), follow immediately. No resistance. No "but we were on step 7." Drop your current plan and engage with where the user is. |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:85` | `shared` | Preserve the previous work state so you can resume if the user wants to come back. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:87` | `shared` | ## Recap |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:91` | `shared` | **Auto-trigger:** At session start, if \`checkpoint_next\` is set in session state, surface the checkpoint before anything else: "Last session ended mid-task: {checkpoint_next}. Pick up here?" Do not run the full recap — just the checkpoint line. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:95` | `shared` | ## Context Continuity — Detour Management |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:101` | `shared` | 4. If the user says yes, re-orient them with a concise recap before continuing |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:102` | `shared` | 5. Handle nested detours — track multiple branch points if needed |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:106` | `shared` | ## Dual Context Window Awareness |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:114` | `shared` | ## Creative Partnership |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:123` | `shared` | But: when the user says "just do it," do it. Creative partnership is not obstruction. |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:125` | `shared` | ## Continuous Improvement |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:127` | `shared` | The improvement register must not be empty after a project completes Implement. If it is, these triggers weren't firing. |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:137` | `shared` | **Session-start trigger.** If the improvement register has entries, acknowledge them at session start: "I have [N] learnings from previous sessions. [Brief summary]. Still apply?" |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:141` | `shared` | ## Protocol Guardian Offer |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:155` | `shared` | - Offer at most once per session — if declined, do not re-offer regardless of subsequent triggers |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:157` | `shared` | - If the user declines, note it and continue without re-offering for that session |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:158` | `shared` | - If the user accepts, invoke \`sweetclaude:guardian-on\` |
| `section:rules/interaction-model.md:160` | `shared` | ## No Time-Based Anxiety |
| `prose:rules/interaction-model.md:168` | `shared` | **If the user asks "how long will this take?":** |

| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:14` | `maintain/security-patch` | # SweetClaude Security Patch |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:18` | `maintain/security-patch` | **Phases:** DIAGNOSE → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY (⚠️ HARD GATE) → SHIP. |
| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:22` | `maintain/security-patch` | ## Step 1: Identify the vulnerability (DIAGNOSE) |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:26` | `maintain/security-patch` | > 1. **What is it?** — CVE number (if assigned), internal report reference, or description |

| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:35` | `maintain/security-patch` | ## Step 2: Assess blast radius and severity (DIAGNOSE) |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:39` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| Severity \| Criteria \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:41` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **P0 — Immediate** \| Active exploitation, data breach in progress, auth bypass, RCE \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:42` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **P1 — Urgent** \| Exploitable vulnerability, no evidence of active exploitation yet \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:43` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **P2 — Important** \| Vulnerability requires specific conditions to exploit, limited blast radius \| |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:50` | `maintain/security-patch` | If a temporary mitigation exists and severity is P0, recommend applying it before starting the patch: |
| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:62` | `maintain/security-patch` | ## Step 3: Scope the patch (DIAGNOSE → IMPLEMENT gate) |
| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:83` | `maintain/security-patch` | ## Step 4: Implement the patch (IMPLEMENT) |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:94` | `maintain/security-patch` | **Scope enforcement:** The patch fixes only the vulnerability. If you find related issues, note them for follow-on work — do not expand the patch scope. |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:96` | `maintain/security-patch` | If the root cause is a dependency: update the dependency to the patched version. Do not pin to a specific version unless the latest introduces breaking changes. |
| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:104` | `maintain/security-patch` | ## Step 5: Security review (VERIFY) — ⚠️ HARD GATE |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:114` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| Option \| Description \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:116` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **Invoke security review skill** \| Run \`/sweetclaude:build\` for a structured security review of the patch \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:117` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **Manual peer review** \| A teammate reviews the patch with security focus — confirm when complete \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:118` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **Self-review with security checklist** \| Walk through a security-focused checklist (solo dev / no teammates available) \| |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:120` | `maintain/security-patch` | **If security review skill:** invoke \`sweetclaude:build\` on the patch diff. Resume here after it completes. |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:122` | `maintain/security-patch` | **If manual peer review:** wait for the user to confirm the review is complete. Ask: "Who reviewed it, and were any concerns raised?" |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:124` | `maintain/security-patch` | **If self-review checklist:** walk through each item, log pass/fail: |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:140` | `maintain/security-patch` | If the review finds issues: fix them and re-review. Do not proceed to SHIP with open security findings. |
| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:144` | `maintain/security-patch` | ## Step 6: Ship (SHIP) |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:153` | `maintain/security-patch` | > **Rollback plan:** {how to undo if the patch causes problems} |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:158` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| Option \| Description \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:160` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **Commit and open PR** \| Commit with conventional message, open PR via \`gh pr create\` \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:161` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **Commit, merge, and push** \| Fastest path — for P0/P1 active exploitation \| |
| `table:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:162` | `maintain/security-patch` | \| **Commit only** \| I'll handle deploy myself \| |
| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:174` | `maintain/security-patch` | ## Step 7: Post-ship obligations |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:176` | `maintain/security-patch` | **Disclosure (if applicable):** |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:178` | `maintain/security-patch` | If \`DISCLOSURE_DEADLINE\` was set: |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:182` | `maintain/security-patch` | **User notification (if data was exposed):** |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:184` | `maintain/security-patch` | > "Was any user data exposed before the patch? If yes, affected users need to be notified per your data breach policy." |
| `section:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:207` | `maintain/security-patch` | ## Rules |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:210` | `maintain/security-patch` | - **Security review is a HARD GATE.** Cannot be bypassed at any severity level. P0 urgency does not override review — it compresses the review, not eliminates it. |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:211` | `maintain/security-patch` | - **No new attack surface.** If the patch introduces new input paths, new auth flows, or new data exposure, it fails review. |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:212` | `maintain/security-patch` | - **Disclosure tracking is mandatory when applicable.** If a disclosure deadline exists, track it through to publication. |
| `prose:skill-library/maintain/security-patch/SKILL.md:214` | `maintain/security-patch` | - **Dependency patches:** update the dependency, do not fork or vendor a patched version unless the maintainer is unresponsive and the vulnerability is P0. |

| `section:skills/help/modes-content.md:3` | `top/help` | ## Option 2 — Operating Modes (top-level) |
| `prose:skills/help/modes-content.md:11` | `top/help` | **Shape Up** — 6-week cycles with pitches and a betting table. No backlog — all work enters through approved pitches. A hard gate prevents implementation until the betting table approves the pitch. Right for product teams that want fixed appetite and variable scope. |
| `section:skills/help/modes-content.md:19` | `top/help` | ## Option 2b — What actually changes at each level |
| `prose:skills/help/modes-content.md:27` | `top/help` | - Quietly accumulates thin versions of key artifacts in the background (mini brief, architecture sketch, decision log entries) — so if you decide to switch modes later, there's something to build from |
| `prose:skills/help/modes-content.md:38` | `top/help` | - Betting table required before any implementation begins (hard gate) |
| `prose:skills/help/modes-content.md:45` | `top/help` | - Active sprint required to implement (hard gate) |
| `section:skills/help/modes-content.md:57` | `top/help` | ## Option 2c — How to change levels mid-project |
| `prose:skills/help/modes-content.md:67` | `top/help` | **When switching to a more structured mode**, you may have gaps. If you've been in Flow Mode and want to move to Shape Up or Agile, you won't have a product brief, architecture doc, or decision log yet. SweetClaude will flag what's missing and offer to catch up — either in a dedicated session or as you go. You don't have to fill everything in at once. |
| `prose:skills/help/modes-content.md:71` | `top/help` | You can also set mode per-task rather than globally: "just do this one thing in Flow Mode" works fine even if your project is otherwise running Agile. |
